This report reveals that in the years following the Civil War, Black Americans faced significant challenges as they attempted to establish themselves as free citizens.

As a tangible expression of their newfound freedom, they acquired property. Black property ownership in Fairfax is a story of perseverance in the face of adversity. The black investors who pioneered African American communities contributed to the enduring black presence in the county.
